description:
## What is unreachable

`Enumerable` declares `slice/1` and three implementations answer it:

```
lib/enumerable.fz:68   fn slice(_list), do: {:error, :unsupported}
lib/enumerable.fz:76   fn slice(map), do: Map.slice(map)
lib/enumerable.fz:85   fn slice(%Range{...}) do ... Range.slice(...) end
```

Nothing calls it. There is no `Enum.slice` in `lib/enum.fz`, and no other caller of `Enumerable.slice` anywhere in `lib/`. `Map.slice/1` and `Range.slice/6` exist only to be reached through it, so they are unreachable too -- `Range.slice/6` is the reason `Range.reverse/2` exists, which is the private helper in fz-5xp.92.

For lists the callback would not help even if something did call it: `List`'s implementation returns `{:error, :unsupported}` unconditionally.

## The choice

Either `Enum.slice/2,3` is coming and this is scaffolding waiting for its consumer, or it is not and this is a protocol callback, three implementations and two helper functions carrying maintenance weight for nobody.

If it is the former, this ticket is a note that the scaffolding predates its consumer and should be finished. If the latter, it is a deletion: the callback, the three `defimpl` bodies, `Map.slice/1`, `Range.slice/6`, and `Range.reverse/2` all go together.

## Found how

Documenting `Enumerable`'s callbacks: writing an honest `@doc` for `slice/1` meant naming the `Enum` function that reaches it, and there is none.
title: Enumerable.slice/1 is surface nothing reaches
